headline: Ship none yet: the {count.passing.pass_rate|words} configurations that hold the {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} pass rate in every task run far past the {criteria.p95.threshold} p95 latency budget.
lede: {arm:brisk-s.high.r1}, the cheaper of the two that hold every task, reads a p95 of {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95} overall, so its slowest task is at least that slow. A budget covering that task, once read, or a Brisk-S fix that lifts multi-hop and ambiguous-entity planning within the budget would change the answer.
flag: Latency was read only over all tasks, never within each one, so the per-task latency gate is inferred from the overall p95, not read.

caveats.label: Latency read only overall
caveats.material_if: only if a task's own p95 sits far below the overall one, enough that a configuration holding the pass rate everywhere comes under {criteria.p95.threshold} in every task; with overall p95 readings of {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95} and {measure.latency_ms.atlas-m.high.r1.p95}, at least one task must miss if the tasks split the cases between them.

caveats.label: Per-task pass rates state no count
caveats.material_if: if the misses of {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} are noise: assuming each task held its traffic share of the cases, its multi-hop miss reads the wrong way {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.task.multihop.wrong_side} of the time and its ambiguous-entity miss {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.task.disamb.wrong_side}. Were both truly to clear, it would hold every task while under the budget overall and become the pick, pending per-task latency.

only in the direction of the hold: {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} is the best of {n_candidates|int} configurations and clears multi-hop by {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.multihop.gap|abs|pts} points, so a fresh run would tend to read it lower and leave only {arm:atlas-m.high.r1}, which clears multi-hop by {criteria.pass_rate.atlas-m.high.r1.multihop.gap|abs|pts} points, holding the pass rate everywhere, at a slower p95.
only for the comparison of the two configurations that hold the pass rate, which reads their own spreads unpaired; the hold compares each configuration with the declared lines, not with a baseline.

decision.text: Hold: {count.surviving|words} of the {count.arms|int} configurations clear both gates. The {count.undecided|words} left undecided are so only because latency was never read within a task, and both run past the budget overall.

{arm:brisk-s.high.r1} holds every task's pass rate but reads a p95 of {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95} overall; {arm:atlas-m.high.r1} holds it too at {measure.latency_ms.atlas-m.high.r1.p95} and, as this run's unnamed provider routing served it, costs {cost.gap.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.multiple} as much.
{arm:brisk-s.low.r1}, the closest within the budget overall at {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95}, misses the pass rate on multi-hop and on ambiguous entities.

{arm:brisk-s.high.r1} clears multi-hop by only {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.multihop.gap|abs|pts} points, ambiguous entities by {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.disamb.gap|abs|pts} and date math by {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.datemath.gap|abs|pts}. If each task held its traffic share of the cases, a run this size would read them on the wrong side {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.task.multihop.wrong_side}, {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.task.disamb.wrong_side} and {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.task.datemath.wrong_side} of the time.

On the other side of the hold, {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} misses multi-hop by {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.multihop.gap|abs|pts} points and ambiguous entities by {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.disamb.gap|abs|pts}, and sits on the line in date math. On the same assumed counts these read the wrong way {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.task.multihop.wrong_side}, {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.task.disamb.wrong_side} and {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.task.datemath.wrong_side} of the time; a rerun there could turn the hold into a pick.
First, p95 latency read within each task for the configurations nearest both lines; then the latency owner declaring whether the {criteria.p95.threshold} budget is firm.

claims.text: Only {count.passing.pass_rate|words} of the {count.arms|int} configurations hold the {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} pass rate in every task, both at high reasoning with a retry; every other configuration falls short on multi-hop.

evidence.caption: Pass rate by task for the six configurations nearest the {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} gate; the rest sit further below it.

claims.text: Both run far past the {criteria.p95.threshold} latency budget overall, and since a configuration's slowest task is at least as slow as the whole, each misses the budget in at least one task.

evidence.caption: Latency from p50 to p95 over all tasks, against the {criteria.p95.threshold} budget the gate sets within each task.

claims.text: Every configuration under the budget overall misses the pass rate in at least one task; the closest, {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}, misses multi-hop by {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.multihop.gap|abs|pts} points and ambiguous entities by {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.disamb.gap|abs|pts}, and sits exactly on the line in date math.

evidence.caption: Pass rate by task for the ten configurations whose overall p95 is under the {criteria.p95.threshold} budget, against the {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} gate.

Kept failures of the closest configuration, one each from multi-hop, date math and ambiguous entities: the first collapses two hops into one query, the second is an off-by-one date window in a task it holds exactly on the line, the third answers an ambiguous name without asking. How many failures each was kept from is not stated; they show kinds of failure, not shares.

claims.text: Of the two that hold the pass rate, {arm:atlas-m.high.r1} costs {cost.gap.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.multiple} as much as {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} as this run served them, with no provider named for either, so the ratio may not hold under another routing; their pass rates are not told apart.

evidence.caption: Cost per 1,000 calls at this run's unnamed routing. If the declared monthly volume counts calls, Atlas-M costs {cost.gap.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.monthly|abs|usd_whole} more a month; if it counts tasks, which each make more than one call, the gap is larger.
Pass rate change moving from Atlas-M to Brisk-S at high reasoning with a retry, computed before the rates are rounded, with its unpaired interval, which crosses zero.

explore.binds: Which configurations can ship at all
explore.outcome: Below {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95}, no budget admits a configuration that holds the pass rate everywhere. To admit {arm:brisk-s.high.r1}, the budget must cover its slowest task's p95, which is at least that overall figure and not yet read.

explore.binds: Whether a configuration within the budget qualifies
explore.outcome: At a line of {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.multihop.value} or lower, {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} holds every task while staying under the budget overall; above it, no configuration within the budget does.

omitted.why: Each misses the pass rate in every task; they appear only in the under-budget table.
The gate reads each task; the overall rate hides the multi-hop shortfall that decides it.

omitted.what: Retry and reasoning effects across the whole grid
omitted.why: A retry raises the pass rate in every configuration; the grid's effects describe how the two leading configurations were reached, not which ships. They stay in the appendix.

omitted.what: Calls per task and p50 latency
omitted.why: Neither is gated, and neither changes which configuration clears both lines.
The snapshot holds no figures for them.

next.text: Read p95 latency within each task for {arm:brisk-s.high.r1}, {arm:atlas-m.high.r1} and {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}.
next.settles: Whether the latency gate fails in each task as the overall p95 implies, how high a budget would have to go to admit the configurations that hold the pass rate, and whether single lookups, {task.single.share} of traffic, could go to a configuration within the budget while the harder tasks go elsewhere.

next.text: The latency owner declares whether the {criteria.p95.threshold} budget is firm. To admit {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} it would have to rise to at least {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95}, its exact level pending the per-task read.
next.settles: Whether {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} is a candidate at all; if it is, it costs less than the only other configuration that holds every task.

next.text: Rerun {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} on multi-hop and ambiguous-entity cases: confirming its misses four times in five takes about {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.task.multihop.cases_needed_two_sided_80|int} and {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.task.disamb.cases_needed_two_sided_80|int} cases respectively, on assumed task counts.
next.settles: Whether the closest configuration within the budget truly misses, or holds every task and becomes the pick.

next.text: Fix Brisk-S's multi-hop decomposition and its clarifying question on ambiguous names at low reasoning with a retry, then rerun those two tasks.
next.settles: Whether a configuration within the budget can hold the pass rate everywhere, which would make it the pick.

next.text: If the budget rises, rerun {arm:brisk-s.high.r1} on fresh multi-hop cases: confirming its thin clearance four times in five takes about {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.task.multihop.cases_needed_two_sided_80|int} cases, on assumed task counts.
next.settles: Whether its multi-hop pass rate truly clears the gate or was the luck of the best of many.

method.text: {count.arms|int} configurations crossing {count.levels.model|words} models, {count.levels.reasoning|words} reasoning levels and retry on or off, each run on {scoreboard.brisk-s.high.r1.cases|int} cases with none lost. There is no baseline configuration.

Single lookup, multi-hop, date and unit math, and ambiguous entity, with traffic shares of {task.single.share}, {task.multihop.share}, {task.datemath.share} and {task.disamb.share}. Cases per task are not stated; case counts and wrong-side odds quoted for reruns assume each task held its traffic share of the cases.
The campaign does not define a pass in words; the failure cards compare the planner's tool calls and arguments with the expected ones.
Pass rate at least {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} in each task, and p95 latency at most {criteria.p95.threshold} in each task. Both are read on point estimates; per-task pass rates carry no interval.
Only p50 and p95 over all tasks were recorded, so the per-task latency gate has no figure for any configuration. A configuration's slowest task has a p95 at least as high as its overall one.
The one interval shown is {lever.model.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.level}, unpaired, from each configuration's binomial spread over its cases; it reads wider than a paired one would.

Cost per 1,000 calls as this run was served; no provider is named for any configuration, so the routing behind the costs is unknown and the cost order may not hold under another. Monthly figures use the declared volume of {meta.volume_per_month|int}, read as calls; the campaign does not say what it counts. How many trials reported a cost is not stated.
